items.title: 63477_Joe Darensbourg oral history interview
items.q: Fritz and Jimmie Noone was two of my favorite players in those days.

ctx.x: When you talk about technique, do you mean actually knowing what he was doing on the horn, or facility?
By the way he played and the tone. I could tell in those days. Fritz and Jimmie Noone was two of my favorite players in those days.

items.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18
items.q: Just playing with Jimmy New York? He was playing saxophone.

ctx.x: The first time I picked up a saxophone, I could play it. Oh yeah? Yeah. But, also singing is quite different. From a clarinet? Yeah. Well, all, all saxophones, things are the same for that matter. But, uh, it's different from a clarinet. Still in all, if you can play a clarinet, you can play a saxophone. Something real easy, because the clarinet is a lot more difficult instrument than a saxophone. But I had, uh, and I had food with a saxophone before, a little bit, you know, because my teacher was a saxophone…
Joe Poston? Yeah. Just playing with Jimmy New York? He was playing saxophone. Yeah? Yeah.

And Zooty, Zooty had been around St. Louis just before then. It was really in Chicago last time. Well, Zooty had been playing in St. Louis though, I hadn't been playing with those guys, but they was talking about him. Then I played around there for a long, uh, not, well, not too long. Then I went to, uh, Harrisburg, Illinois with, with a bunch of guys and started working for these gangsters, Charlie Berger and his gang.
